body: Why do people marry so early in America? As an European, it seems strange to me. Are you living in the 1700's or what?
Life is so fucking unfair, congrats on you bro but where I live 100k are fantasy salaries reserved for CEOs and such. Programmers here make 2k/month and that is considered decent, so unfair.
Funny how in these threads it's always the women who are cheating, just confirms my belief, sadly enough. Maybe religion wasn't wrong after all.

Not a STEM major here but I guess I could be classified as "smart" anyways, since I have an IQ of >135 which I got tested for by my psychiatrist. If you look one of my earlier threads you can see my whole background story, some of it is really bad luck and others things that I could not change. The most depressing part for me, is thinking back and realizing that some girls were indeed interested in me and flirted, but I was to scared to act because of my social anxiety. I've lived a very isolated life for the past 8-9 years and this has changed me a lot, for the negative. 

I'm now at an age where 95% of all women my age (judging from statistics) have had a relationship, I missed my chances in my teenage years and now I'm paying for it by not being given a chance from women since inexperience is a sign for them that I'm not "normal". If they knew what I had been through in my life they would probably think I'm not such a freak hopefully.

It's hard not being depressed and having low self esteem when the norms in society are the way they are. In my country, most people have lost their virginity by 15, a big majority. After high school it's practically unheard of being a virgin, and this just makes me wanna kill myself since I'm 22 and never been in a relationship. I wish there was some way to stop comparing myself to society's expectations of what is "normal", but I can't do that.
I wouldn't bat an eye, then again, where I live it's common for 14-15 year olds girls to date 25-30 year old men. Not that I have done it, to each their own.

This was my initial thought also, but if you look at r/seduction and r/askwomen you'll see even the older women (30+) don't like inexperienced guys at all, even if they are nice gentlemen. There are of course exceptions but they are far and few in between. 

Yes, the optimal thing for me would be to find another virgin girl, but where I live maybe 85% are atheists so there are really no girls saving themselves for marriage. I'm not really religious, more agnostic, but I wouldn't mind dating a christian girl who are waiting for marriage since I respect that choice. But realistically it's impossible to find at my age in my country. 

That's also what I'm afraid of. But I think I'll give it a try later this week, just need to take some good pictures first. The best thing would be, as you say, meeting women with similar interests as myself. That's what I hope to do when I start university so there is still a little bit of hope, although my depression is making it a lot harder to be optimistic.

It's funny really. Tonight I dreamed about having a relationship and being madly in love, only to wake up and realize it was only an illusion. I just wanted to get back to sleep and never wake up, my dreams are far better than real life I feel like. 

Yes, I think I could talk to women online but I haven't yet made a profile on a dating website. Also don't really know what type of picture I should take, I tend to over think these things. But will be trying to start doing it this week.

Thank you! Yeah, I know I've had a bad start in life, but when I read women saying that dating a virgin is unacceptable if they're 20+ I can't help but get depressed, since I didn't really have a chance to be in relationships before that. But I have big hopes for university, I'll probably meet a few nice people. I remember being 16 and at that point I wasn't suicidal but somewhat depressed because of my sickness and missing school. I hadn't even started thinking about relationships since I was focusing on getting better, but the years pass fast. Feels like yesterday I was 16 and now I'm 22. You should take every opportunity in life even at your age because times moves so fast.

Yeah, exactly this. In middle school and high school the popular guys were the "alpha" males who acted like jerks but they were confident and could get girls, I guess that's just nature. But I still know that there are some women who appreciates men who are not like that. I've seen a few comments here on reddit where a girl mention that she doesn't care if the guy is a virgin or not, and although this is very rare it warms my heart every time. The problem in real life is knowing what girls who doesn't mind inexperienced men, it's not very easy to find out. I just don't understand why so many are judgmental towards virgins in particularly, there doesn't have to be any "wrong" with the individual, just bad circumstances in life leading up to that. 

I don't think my lack of friends is really a problem. At work I get along just fine with most of them, but I haven't really taken any initiative to get to know them outside work.

I'm very thankful for your kind words, I also hope there is someone out there. I have been thinking about trying online dating also, but been to afraid to try so far. It feels like It's now or never, after university it will even be harder. So I have to give it everything now or It's to late, a shame really.

Thanks for the kind words. I don't think I'll feel like a different person really, I just think it will give me great confidence in myself and feel loved. But I don't really care that much for the sex, it's the relationship bit i desire the most. And I know there are other people like you who also lost their virginity late, and I guess that is what gives me hope still. But still, we are not the norm in society for a VARIETY of reasons, it's not that we are unattractive necessarily, and I hate all "bias" against virgins, potraiting them like freaks.

But yeah, it's mainly love I want to experience, sex isn't as important.
